text: The Pope! How many divisions has he got?
variants: How many divisions does the Pope have?
documented_in: Winston Churchill, The Second World War, vol. 1 (1948), ch. 8, p. 105: Stalin's sarcastic reply in 1935 when Pierre Laval asked him to ease the treatment of Russian Catholics to win the Pope's favour. A second report is in the diary of US Assistant Press Secretary Eban Ayers, 24 January 1946. Both are secondhand; Churchill was not present. Checked: https://en.wikiquote.org/wiki/Joseph_Stalin
lens: Ask what force actually stands behind a claim of authority, and don't be moved by one that has none. But the line cuts both ways: the Church outlasted the Soviet Union, so check whether you are mistaking an absence of divisions for an absence of power.
impact_rationale: The classic statement of hard-power realism, made sharper by history's answer to it; useful in any contest between force and legitimacy.
counter_sayings: The ruler is the boat and the people are the water; water can carry the boat, and water can overturn it.
